This notebook has one job: build UC Davis civilian-arrival profiles from the
UC Davis extract (`data/baseline_civilian_profiles_uc_davis.csv`), and check
that the underlying data supports the values that go into it. The Patient
Surge Model app does not read this file directly: its predefined civilian
profiles are the checked-in `data/baseline_civilian_profiles*.csv` files
(see `civilian_profile_file()` in `R/app/mod_profiles.R`), and its surge
"UC Davis calibrated profiles" option is the NDMS-based
`deloitte_test_profile_config()` in `R/shared/profiles_deloitte.R`.
Everything here follows the flow structure and calibration formulas of
`2026_Assessing_the_hospital_occupancy_under_a_surge_event/main.tex`
(Sections 2.2 and 2.5), restricted to the app's reduced three-unit
configuration (ICU, GenMed = Davis' Med-Surg/Tele, Surge = Davis' IP Surge)
and restricted to what the data actually contains -- no parameter is filled
in from an external/illustrative source.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(readxl)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(fitdistrplus)
Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "English")
```

# 1. Load and merge Davis data into one unified daily table

All four source sheets are merged once, by date, into a single wide table
`davis_daily` (one row per day, uppercase column names): `Capacity` and
`ADT Summary` and `ICU DownUp` from the IMPACTS extract, plus
`Patient Surge Model ED Data` from the separate ED workbook. Every later
section -- consistency checks and parameter calibration alike -- reads from
this one table (or `davis_long`, its per-unit reshape below), instead of
each rebuilding its own merge.

```{r, warning=FALSE}
impacts_path <- "davis_data/IMPACTS Data Extract_V2_Jun25.xlsx"
ed_path <- "davis_data/Patient and Viral Surge Data_V4.xlsx"

raw_capacity <- readxl::read_excel(impacts_path, sheet = "Capacity")
raw_adt <- readxl::read_excel(impacts_path, sheet = "ADT Summary") |>
  dplyr::rename(DAY_DT = DateValue)
raw_icu_downup <- readxl::read_excel(impacts_path, sheet = "ICU DownUp") |>
  dplyr::rename(DAY_DT = Transfer_Date)
raw_ed <- readxl::read_excel(ed_path, sheet = "Patient Surge Model ED Data") |>
  dplyr::rename(DAY_DT = ED_ARRIVAL_IMPUTED_DT)

parse_day <- function(x) as.Date(lubridate::parse_date_time(x, c("%d/%m/%Y", "%m/%d/%Y", "%Y-%m-%d")))

davis_daily <- raw_capacity |>
  dplyr::mutate(DAY_DT = parse_day(DAY_DT)) |>
  dplyr::full_join(raw_adt |> dplyr::mutate(DAY_DT = parse_day(DAY_DT)), by = "DAY_DT") |>
  dplyr::full_join(raw_icu_downup |> dplyr::mutate(DAY_DT = parse_day(DAY_DT)), by = "DAY_DT") |>
  dplyr::full_join(raw_ed |> dplyr::mutate(DAY_DT = parse_day(DAY_DT)), by = "DAY_DT") |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-DAY_DT, ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.)))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(DAY_DT)

names(davis_daily) <- toupper(names(davis_daily))

davis_daily <- davis_daily |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    YEAR = factor(format(DAY_DT, "%Y"), levels = c("2020", "2021", "2022", "2023", "2024", "2025")),
    DAY = factor(weekdays(DAY_DT),
                 levels = c("Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday")),
    MONTH = factor(months(DAY_DT),
                   levels = c("January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July",
                              "August", "September", "October", "November", "December")),
    AVERAGE_ED_WAITING_INTERVAL_DAYS = AVERAGE_ED_WAITING_INTERVAL / 1440,
    AVERAGE_ED_BOARDING_INTERVAL_DAYS = AVERAGE_ED_BOARDING_INTERVAL / 1440
  )

# The app's reduced unit set and the Davis column-suffix each maps to. Note
# AvgLengthOfStay's Med-Surg/Tele column is the one Davis field using the
# short suffix "MED" instead of "MED_SURG_TELE" -- every other field
# (Admit_, Discharges_, OCC_BEDS_, ...) uses the full suffix. This map is the
# single place that quirk needs to be handled.
unit_map <- c(ICU = "ICU", GenMed = "MED_SURG_TELE", Surge = "IP_SURGE")
los_col <- c(ICU = "AVGLENGTHOFSTAY_ICU", GenMed = "AVGLENGTHOFSTAY_MED", Surge = "AVGLENGTHOFSTAY_IP_SURGE")

davis_daily_2025 <- davis_daily |> dplyr::filter(YEAR %in% c("2024", "2025"))
```

# 2. Reshape to a per-unit long table (for consistency checks)

```{r}
reshape_units <- function(data, cols, prefix, value_name) {
  data |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c("DAY_DT", "YEAR", "DAY", "MONTH", cols))) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = dplyr::all_of(cols), names_to = "Unit", values_to = value_name) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Unit = stringr::str_remove(Unit, paste0("^", prefix)))
}

vars_adm <- c("ICU", "MED_SURG_TELE", "IP_SURGE")
tt_beds_cols <- paste0("TTL_BEDS_", vars_adm)
admit_cols <- paste0("ADMIT_", vars_adm)
discharge_cols <- paste0("DISCHARGES_", vars_adm)
occ_cols <- paste0("OCC_BEDS_", vars_adm)
los_cols <- unname(los_col)

davis_long <- purrr::reduce(
  list(
    reshape_units(davis_daily, tt_beds_cols, "TTL_BEDS_", "tt_beds"),
    reshape_units(davis_daily, admit_cols, "ADMIT_", "admitted"),
    reshape_units(davis_daily, discharge_cols, "DISCHARGES_", "discharges"),
    reshape_units(davis_daily, occ_cols, "OCC_BEDS_", "occupied"),
    reshape_units(davis_daily, los_cols, "AVGLENGTHOFSTAY_", "los") |>
      dplyr::mutate(Unit = ifelse(Unit == "MED", "MED_SURG_TELE", Unit))
  ),
  dplyr::full_join, by = c("DAY_DT", "YEAR", "DAY", "MONTH", "Unit")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(occupied_pct = 100 * occupied / tt_beds)
```

```{r}
annual_occupancy <- davis_long |>
  dplyr::group_by(YEAR, Unit) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_days = sum(!is.na(occupied)),
    mean_occupied = mean(occupied, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_total_beds = mean(tt_beds, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_occupied_pct = mean(occupied_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

annual_occupancy_weighted <- davis_long |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(occupied), !is.na(tt_beds), tt_beds > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(YEAR, Unit) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    annual_occupancy_pct = 100 * sum(occupied) / sum(tt_beds),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```


# 3. Data consistency checks

## Length-of-stay distribution vs. a fitted log-normal

Sanity check that the log-normal CV used for each unit's CV_values in the
profile CSV is a reasonable fit to the observed daily-average LOS series
(a proxy for patient-level dispersion, since only day-level averages are
available -- see the caveat on `fit_lognormal_cv()` below).

```{r, warning=FALSE}
fit_lognormal_cv <- function(x) {
  fit <- MASS::fitdistr(stats::na.omit(x), "lognormal")
  sigma <- unname(fit$estimate["sdlog"])
  sqrt(exp(sigma^2) - 1)
}

lognormal_fit_2025 <- davis_long |>
  dplyr::filter(YEAR  %in% c("2024", "2025"), !is.na(los), los > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(Unit) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_los = mean(los), cv = fit_lognormal_cv(los), .groups = "drop")
lognormal_fit_2025

davis_long |> dplyr::filter(YEAR  %in% c("2024", "2025")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = los,y=after_stat(density))) +
  geom_freqpoly(binwidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~Unit, scales = "free") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 30)) +
  labs(title = "2025 length-of-stay distribution by unit", x = "Length of stay (days)", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Occupancy over time

```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=9}
ggplot(davis_long, aes(x = DAY_DT, y = occupied_pct, color = Unit)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Unit, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Occupancy (% of total beds) by unit", x = NULL, y = "Occupied (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## ICU transfer counts vs. Little's Law (used by the transfer-rate calibration below)

The `ICU DownUp` sheet's per-unit transfer counts feed directly into
`calibrate_transfer_rates()` below. Before trusting them, cross-check them
against occupancy and LOS via Little's Law: a single tracked outflow column
cannot legitimately exceed the unit's total implied departure rate.

```{r}
inflow_cols <- c("ED_TO_ICU", "MED_SURG_TELE_TO_ICU", "NICU_TO_ICU", "PEDS_TO_ICU", "PICU_TO_ICU",
                  "WMN_PAV_TO_ICU", "OBSTETRICS_TO_ICU", "IP_SURGE_TO_ICU")
outflow_cols <- c("ICU_TO_ED", "ICU_TO_MED_SURG_TELE", "ICU_TO_NICU", "ICU_TO_PEDS", "ICU_TO_PICU",
                   "ICU_TO_WMN_PAV", "ICU_TO_OBSTETRICS", "ICU_TO_IP_SURGE")

total_inflow_tracked <- sum(sapply(inflow_cols, function(cn) mean(davis_daily_2025[[cn]], na.rm = TRUE)))
total_outflow_tracked <- sum(sapply(outflow_cols, function(cn) mean(davis_daily_2025[[cn]], na.rm = TRUE)))
icu_occupancy <- mean(davis_daily_2025$OCC_BEDS_ICU, na.rm = TRUE)
icu_los <- mean(davis_daily_2025$AVGLENGTHOFSTAY_ICU, na.rm = TRUE)
littles_law_departure_rate <- icu_occupancy / icu_los
icu_to_medsurg <- mean(davis_daily_2025$ICU_TO_MED_SURG_TELE, na.rm = TRUE)

cat(sprintf("Tracked ICU inflow (sum of *_TO_ICU)   = %.2f/day\n", total_inflow_tracked))
cat(sprintf("Tracked ICU outflow (sum of ICU_TO_*)  = %.2f/day\n", total_outflow_tracked))
cat(sprintf("ADMIT_ICU                               = %.2f/day\n", mean(davis_daily_2025$ADMIT_ICU, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("DISCHARGES_ICU (hospital exit from ICU) = %.2f/day\n", mean(davis_daily_2025$DISCHARGES_ICU, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Little's Law implied total departures   = OCC_BEDS_ICU / LOS = %.2f/%.2f = %.2f/day\n",
            icu_occupancy, icu_los, littles_law_departure_rate))
cat(sprintf("ICU_TO_MED_SURG_TELE alone               = %.2f/day (%.0f%% of the Little's-Law total)\n",
            icu_to_medsurg, 100 * icu_to_medsurg / littles_law_departure_rate))
cat("=> Internally inconsistent: ICU-linked transfer rates below (eps_S, eps_M) should be read as\n",
    "   approximate, not validated, until this is resolved.\n")
```

## What the data does NOT support

Checked directly against the raw sheet columns (`Capacity`, `ADT Summary`,
`ICU DownUp`, `Patient Surge Model ED Data`):

- **No per-unit split between ED-origin and direct/transfer admissions.**
  `ADT Summary`'s `Admit_<unit>` is a single total per unit, combining all
  admission sources. `Accpt_Trnsfrs_ICU_*` / `Accpt_Trnsfrs_Non_ICU_*` exist,
  but only split by ICU/non-ICU and age group (Peds/Adult/Unspecified), not
  by destination unit (GenMed vs. Surge) -- so the paper's $A_S, A_M, A_I$
  (external inflows bypassing ED) cannot be calibrated separately from ED
  admissions with this extract. Every admission below is therefore modeled
  as `ED -> unit`, matching how `Admit_<unit>` was already used before this
  reorganization -- not because every admission is truly ED-origin, but
  because the data does not let ED-origin and direct admissions be told
  apart.
- **No Med-Surg/Tele <-> IP Surge transfer counts.** `ICU DownUp` only
  tracks flows into/out of ICU; a direct Surge<->GenMed transfer is not
  observed in either direction. `calibrate_transfer_rates()` below sets both
  `varphi_M` (Surge -> GenMed) and `psi_S` (GenMed -> Surge) to 0 rather than
  substituting a value from elsewhere.
- **ICU-linked transfer counts are internally inconsistent** with a
  Little's-Law check on ICU's own occupancy and LOS (see above) -- so
  `eps_S`/`eps_M` (ICU -> Surge / ICU -> GenMed), while used, should be
  treated as approximate.

# 4. ED parameters (2025)

```{r}
min_to_day <- 1 / 1440

ed_param <- function(x_min) {
  x_days <- x_min * min_to_day
  m <- mean(x_days, na.rm = TRUE)
  s <- stats::sd(x_days, na.rm = TRUE)
  data.frame(mean_days = m, sd_days = s, cv = s / m, median_days = stats::median(x_days, na.rm = TRUE))
}

ed_parameters_2025 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  waiting = ed_param(davis_daily_2025$AVERAGE_ED_WAITING_INTERVAL),
  los = ed_param(davis_daily_2025$AVERAGE_ED_LOS_INTERVAL),
  boarding = ed_param(davis_daily_2025$AVERAGE_ED_BOARDING_INTERVAL),
  .id = "interval"
)
ed_arrivals_2025 <- davis_daily_2025 |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_arrivals_per_day = mean(DAILY_ED_ARRIVALS, na.rm = TRUE),
                    median_arrivals_per_day = median(DAILY_ED_ARRIVALS, na.rm = TRUE),
                    mean_lwbt_per_day = mean(DAILY_LWBT_COUNT, na.rm = TRUE))

ed_parameters_2025
ed_arrivals_2025

# Patient Surge Model input for the "ED" pathway step: door-to-provider wait
# time, used as the ED step's mean LOS/CV. ED *boarding* is not a model
# input -- it is produced by the model once ED is chained to GenMed/ICU/
# Surge, and the observed AVERAGE_ED_BOARDING_INTERVAL is kept only as an
# external validation target to compare simulated boarding against.
ed_step_los_days <- ed_parameters_2025$mean_days[ed_parameters_2025$interval == "waiting"]
ed_step_cv <- ed_parameters_2025$cv[ed_parameters_2025$interval == "waiting"]
cat(sprintf("ED step (model input): mean LOS = %.4f days, CV = %.4f\n", ed_step_los_days, ed_step_cv))
cat(sprintf("Validation target (NOT a model input): observed mean ED boarding = %.4f days (CV = %.4f)\n",
            ed_parameters_2025$mean_days[ed_parameters_2025$interval == "boarding"],
            ed_parameters_2025$cv[ed_parameters_2025$interval == "boarding"]))
```

# 5. Parameter calibration (paper Section 2.5)

Every function below reads only from `davis_daily_2025`/`ed_parameters_2025`/
`ed_arrivals_2025`; nothing is filled in from the paper's Appendix or any
other non-Davis source.

```{r}
# Returns 0 (with a warning) instead of erroring when a Davis extract column
# is absent, so a genuinely missing field reads as "not observed", not a
# crash.
col_sum <- function(data, col) {
  if (!col %in% names(data)) {
    warning(sprintf("Column '%s' not found; treating its contribution as 0.", col))
    return(0)
  }
  sum(data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
}
col_mean <- function(data, col) {
  if (!col %in% names(data)) {
    warning(sprintf("Column '%s' not found; treating its contribution as 0.", col))
    return(0)
  }
  mean(data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
}

# sigma (ED -> treatment), xi (boarding -> admission), omega (LWBS); paper
# Section 2.5.1.
calibrate_ed_rates <- function(ed_parameters, ed_arrivals) {
  mean_wait_days <- max(ed_parameters$mean_days[ed_parameters$interval == "waiting"], 1e-6)
  mean_board_days <- max(ed_parameters$mean_days[ed_parameters$interval == "boarding"], 1e-6)

  sigma <- 1 / mean_wait_days
  xi <- 1 / mean_board_days

  f <- ed_arrivals$mean_lwbt_per_day / ed_arrivals$mean_arrivals_per_day
  f <- min(max(f, 0), 0.9999)
  omega <- sigma * f / max(1 - f, 1e-9)

  data.frame(
    parameter = c("sigma", "omega", "xi"),
    value = c(sigma, omega, xi),
    description = c(
      "ED -> treatment rate (1/mean waiting time)",
      "LWBS rate (competing-exponential with sigma)",
      "Boarding -> admission rate (1/mean boarding time, common to all units)"
    )
  )
}

# p_S, p_M, p_I: proportion of treated ED patients admitted to each unit,
# using total Admit_<unit> as the numerator (no ED-specific admit count
# exists -- see "What the data does NOT support" above) and observed
# seen-total (arrivals - LWBS) as the denominator. q = p_S + p_M + p_I.
calibrate_admission_proportions <- function(davis_daily_2025, unit_map) {
  seen_total <- sum(davis_daily_2025$DAILY_ED_ARRIVALS, na.rm = TRUE) -
    sum(davis_daily_2025$DAILY_LWBT_COUNT, na.rm = TRUE)

  proportions <- lapply(names(unit_map), function(model_unit) {
    p <- col_sum(davis_daily_2025, paste0("ADMIT_", unit_map[[model_unit]])) / seen_total
    data.frame(unit = model_unit, p = p)
  }) |> dplyr::bind_rows()

  proportions$q <- sum(proportions$p)
  proportions
}

# gamma: treatment completion rate, backed out from mean ED LOS since
# treatment time is not directly measured.
calibrate_treatment_rate <- function(ed_rates, admission_proportions, mean_los_days) {
  mean_wait_days <- 1 / ed_rates$value[ed_rates$parameter == "sigma"]
  mean_board_days <- 1 / ed_rates$value[ed_rates$parameter == "xi"]
  q <- admission_proportions$q[1]
  mean_service_days <- mean_los_days - mean_wait_days - q * mean_board_days
  data.frame(parameter = "gamma", value = 1 / mean_service_days,
             description = "Treatment completion rate (1/mean treatment time)")
}

# varphi (from Surge), psi (from GenMed), epsilon (from ICU): flow-balance
# estimator r_XY = transitions(X -> Y) / bed-days(X), paper Section 2.5.2.
# varphi_M (Surge -> GenMed) and psi_S (GenMed -> Surge) are 0: that
# transfer is not tracked in either direction in this extract (see "What the
# data does NOT support" above) -- not filled in from any other source.
calibrate_transfer_rates <- function(davis_daily_2025) {
  bed_days_S <- col_sum(davis_daily_2025, "OCC_BEDS_IP_SURGE")
  bed_days_M <- col_sum(davis_daily_2025, "OCC_BEDS_MED_SURG_TELE")
  bed_days_I <- col_sum(davis_daily_2025, "OCC_BEDS_ICU")

  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(from_unit = "Surge", to_unit = "GenMed", parameter = "varphi_M",
               value = 0, observed = FALSE, note = "Surge <-> GenMed not tracked in the Davis extract"),
    data.frame(from_unit = "Surge", to_unit = "ICU", parameter = "varphi_I",
               value = col_sum(davis_daily_2025, "IP_SURGE_TO_ICU") / bed_days_S, observed = TRUE, note = NA),
    data.frame(from_unit = "Surge", to_unit = "Discharge", parameter = "varphi_D",
               value = col_sum(davis_daily_2025, "DISCHARGES_IP_SURGE") / bed_days_S, observed = TRUE, note = NA),

    data.frame(from_unit = "GenMed", to_unit = "Surge", parameter = "psi_S",
               value = 0, observed = FALSE, note = "GenMed <-> Surge not tracked in the Davis extract"),
    data.frame(from_unit = "GenMed", to_unit = "ICU", parameter = "psi_I",
               value = col_sum(davis_daily_2025, "MED_SURG_TELE_TO_ICU") / bed_days_M, observed = TRUE, note = NA),
    data.frame(from_unit = "GenMed", to_unit = "Discharge", parameter = "psi_D",
               value = col_sum(davis_daily_2025, "DISCHARGES_MED_SURG_TELE") / bed_days_M, observed = TRUE, note = NA),

    data.frame(from_unit = "ICU", to_unit = "Surge", parameter = "eps_S",
               value = col_sum(davis_daily_2025, "ICU_TO_IP_SURGE") / bed_days_I, observed = TRUE,
               note = "Approximate: fails the Little's-Law check above"),
    data.frame(from_unit = "ICU", to_unit = "GenMed", parameter = "eps_M",
               value = col_sum(davis_daily_2025, "ICU_TO_MED_SURG_TELE") / bed_days_I, observed = TRUE,
               note = "Approximate: fails the Little's-Law check above"),
    data.frame(from_unit = "ICU", to_unit = "Discharge", parameter = "eps_D",
               value = col_sum(davis_daily_2025, "DISCHARGES_ICU") / bed_days_I, observed = TRUE, note = NA)
  )
}

# Top-level: runs all of the above and returns one tidy list of data frames.
calibrate_paper_parameters_davis <- function(davis_daily_2025, ed_parameters, ed_arrivals, unit_map) {
  ed_rates <- calibrate_ed_rates(ed_parameters, ed_arrivals)
  admission_proportions <- calibrate_admission_proportions(davis_daily_2025, unit_map)
  mean_los_days <- ed_parameters$mean_days[ed_parameters$interval == "los"]
  gamma <- calibrate_treatment_rate(ed_rates, admission_proportions, mean_los_days)
  transfer_rates <- calibrate_transfer_rates(davis_daily_2025)

  list(
    ed_rates = dplyr::bind_rows(ed_rates, gamma),
    admission_proportions = admission_proportions,
    transfer_rates = transfer_rates
  )
}
```

```{r}
paper_parameters_davis <- calibrate_paper_parameters_davis(
  davis_daily_2025 = davis_daily_2025,
  ed_parameters = ed_parameters_2025,
  ed_arrivals = ed_arrivals_2025,
  unit_map = unit_map
)

paper_parameters_davis$ed_rates
paper_parameters_davis$admission_proportions
paper_parameters_davis$transfer_rates
```

# 6. Build UC Davis civilian profiles

Builds `data/baseline_civilian_profiles_uc_davis.csv`, in the same
`Profile, Patients_per_day, Pathway, Mean_stays_days, CV_values` schema as
`data/baseline_civilian_profiles.csv` (see `R/app/mod_baseline.R`). Every
patient is modeled as `ED -> <unit>[-> <second unit>]` -- a single entry
type, since the data cannot distinguish ED-origin from direct/transfer
admissions (Section 3 above). A patient's unit sequence has at most one
transfer (matching the app's existing profile depth): the destination (a
second unit, or discharge) is chosen with the competing-exponential
probability $r_{XY} / \sum_Z r_{XZ}$ from `calibrate_transfer_rates()`, and
the time spent in the first unit is $1 / \sum_Z r_{XZ}$ (same construction
already used for $\omega$ above). If a transfer occurs, the second step's
duration reuses that unit's overall mean LOS, since neither the data nor the
paper separately estimates a residual LOS after transfer.

```{r}
# One row per destination (another unit, or "Discharge") for a given source
# unit, with its routing probability and the mean time spent in the source
# unit before that exit (1 / total exit rate).
unit_exit_branches <- function(transfer_rates, source_unit) {
  rows <- transfer_rates |> dplyr::filter(.data$from_unit == source_unit, .data$value > 0)
  total_rate <- sum(rows$value)
  rows |>
    dplyr::transmute(from_unit, to_unit, probability = value / total_rate,
                      mean_days_in_source = 1 / total_rate)
}

# Same CV convention already used across the app's profile configs (see
# default_cv_for_unit() in R/shared/profiles_deloitte.R): 1 for ICU steps,
# 0.24 otherwise.
cv_for_unit_step <- function(unit) if (unit == "ICU") 1 else 0.24

build_unit_profiles <- function(source_unit, entry_patients_per_day, transfer_rates,
                                 ed_step_los_days, ed_step_cv, second_step_los_days) {
  if (is.na(entry_patients_per_day) || entry_patients_per_day <= 0) return(NULL)
  branches <- unit_exit_branches(transfer_rates, source_unit)

  nr = 2
  purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(branches)), function(i) {
    branch <- branches[i, ]
    transferred <- branch$to_unit != "Discharge"

    units <- c("ED", source_unit, if (transferred) branch$to_unit)
    stays <- c(ed_step_los_days, branch$mean_days_in_source,
               if (transferred) second_step_los_days[[branch$to_unit]])
    cvs <- c(ed_step_cv, cv_for_unit_step(source_unit),
             if (transferred) cv_for_unit_step(branch$to_unit))

    data.frame(
      Profile = paste(c("ED", source_unit, if (transferred) branch$to_unit), collapse = "_"),
      Patients_per_day = round(entry_patients_per_day * branch$probability,nr),
      Pathway = paste(units, collapse = ", "),
      Mean_stays_days = paste(round(stays, nr), collapse = ","),
      CV_values = paste(round(cvs, nr), collapse = ",")
    )
  })
}

build_uc_davis_profiles <- function(davis_daily_2025, paper_parameters_davis, unit_map,
                                     ed_step_los_days, ed_step_cv) {
  second_step_los_days <- stats::setNames(
    sapply(names(unit_map), function(model_unit) col_mean(davis_daily_2025, los_col[[model_unit]])),
    names(unit_map)
  )

  lapply(names(unit_map), function(model_unit) {
    entry_rate <- col_mean(davis_daily_2025, paste0("ADMIT_", unit_map[[model_unit]]))
    build_unit_profiles(model_unit, entry_rate, paper_parameters_davis$transfer_rates,
                        ed_step_los_days, ed_step_cv, second_step_los_days)
  }) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
}
```

```{r}
uc_davis_profiles <- build_uc_davis_profiles(
  davis_daily_2025 = davis_daily_2025,
  paper_parameters_davis = paper_parameters_davis,
  unit_map = unit_map,
  ed_step_los_days = ed_step_los_days,
  ed_step_cv = ed_step_cv
)

uc_davis_profiles

write.csv(uc_davis_profiles, "../data/baseline_civilian_profiles_uc_davis.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Separar los parámetros de cada etapa de las trayectorias.
profile_parameters <- uc_davis_profiles |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    profile_id = dplyr::row_number(),
    Unit = as.character(Pathway),
    mean_los = as.character(Mean_stays_days),
    cv = as.character(CV_values)
  ) |>
  tidyr::separate_longer_delim(
    cols = c(Unit, mean_los, cv),
    delim = ","
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Unit = trimws(Unit),
    mean_los = as.numeric(trimws(mean_los)),
    cv = as.numeric(trimws(cv))
  )

# Mostrar valores únicos sin ceros decimales innecesarios.
format_values <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  values <- sort(unique(x[!is.na(x)]))

  formatted <- formatC(values, format = "f", digits = digits) |>
    sub(pattern = "0+$", replacement = "") |>
    sub(pattern = "\\.$", replacement = "")

  paste(formatted, collapse = ", ")
}

# Estancias de ED.
ed_los <- profile_parameters |>
  dplyr::filter(Unit == "ED") |>
  dplyr::pull(mean_los)

ed_note <- if (length(ed_los) == 0L) {
  ""
} else if (dplyr::n_distinct(ed_los) == 1L) {
  sprintf(
    paste0(
      "The mean length of stay in the emergency department (ED) ",
      "is %s days (approximately %s hours). "
    ),
    format_values(ed_los),
    format_values(ed_los * 24, digits = 2)
  )
} else {
  sprintf(
    "Mean lengths of stay in ED vary by profile: %s days. ",
    format_values(ed_los)
  )
}

# CV por unidad, en el orden en que aparecen en la tabla.
cv_by_unit <- profile_parameters |>
  dplyr::group_by(Unit) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cv_values = format_values(cv),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(Unit, unique(profile_parameters$Unit)))

cv_note <- paste0(
  "The coefficients of variation for LOS by unit are: ",
  paste(
    sprintf("%s (%s)", cv_by_unit$Unit, cv_by_unit$cv_values),
    collapse = "; "
  ),
  ". Multiple values indicate variation across profiles. "
)

table_note <- paste0(
  "\\medskip\n",
  "\\begin{minipage}{0.95\\linewidth}\n",
  "\\footnotesize\n",
  "\\textit{Notes:} ",
  ed_note,
  cv_note,
  "Arrival rates represent expected numbers of patients per day. ",
  "Values are rounded for presentation.\n",
  "\\end{minipage}\n"
)

latex_output <- sub(
  "\\end{table}",
  paste0(table_note, "\\end{table}"),
  as.character(latex_table),
  fixed = TRUE
)

#writeLines(latex_output, "patient_profiles.tex")
cat(latex_output)

```
